chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in

a man who struck another man on the head, causing his tongue to become heavy (impaired), [the ruling is] that all the letters of the alphabet are presented to him, then he is given his blood money according to the letter he failed to articulate.

key_terms.مَا لَمْ يُفْصِحْ بِهِ: What he did not articulate clearly

ai.seo_question: How is the blood money calculated for a person whose speech is impaired but not completely lost due to a head injury?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes a precise legal mechanism for calculating 'diyah' (blood money) for speech impairment, specifically linking the compensation to the number of Arabic consonants lost due to a head injury. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on quantifiable damages ('uqub') and demonstrates how linguistic precision in the Arabic alphabet directly informs financial liability in Islamic law. The ruling underscores the high value placed on clear communication and eloquence in traditional Islamic society.
